pr_title: [FG:InPlacePodVerticalScaling] Implement AllocatedResources status changes for Beta
pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?
/kind feature

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Implement the changes to the `AllocatedResources` container status field for beta, including:
1. The `AllocatedResources` field is only populated if the separate `InPlacePodVerticalScalingAllocatedStatus` feature gate is enabled.
2. The `ContainerStatus.Resources` field is always populated by the Kubelet, even if the container isn't running. For non-running containers, it is set to the allocated resources.
3. Components (including the scheduler & resource quota) use max(spec.resources, status.resources) to compute pod totals.

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:
Fixes https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/128065
Fixes https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/125609
Fixes https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/117765

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?
```release-note
ContainerStatus.AllocatedResources is now guarded by a separate feature gate, InPlacePodVerticalSaclingAllocatedStatus
```

#### Additional documentation e.g., KEPs (Kubernetes Enhancement Proposals), usage docs, etc.:

```docs
- [KEP]: https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-node/1287-in-place-update-pod-resources
```

/sig node
/priority important-soon
/milestone v1.32
/triage accepted

@yujuhong I think this is ready for another review. Here is a summary of the changes since you last reviewed:
- Added 4 new commits, see the aggregate changes here: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/compare/84201658c3560373c47ce159ba3e959d0adadc46..6cb301a56fde608eac00b49ae74e893c0ca76e66
- "fix resize state transitions"
  - if desired resources == allocated resources, then reset the resize status unless a resize is in progress - this makes it so a deferred or infeasible resize can be cleared by rolling back the requested resize
  - always clear the resize status for a terminal pod
  - if allocated == actual, only clear an "in progress" resize status: this prevents a deferred or infeasible resize from being accidentally cleared
- don't clear the resize status when resources are missing - prevents a runtime flake from accidentally clearing the resize status
- If ResourceRequirements changed, always mark a proposed resize - This should fix the test flakes, which were always on test cases that only resized limits. If desired == allocated (the removed check), just let the Kubelet handle clearing the proposed status.
- Don't consider allocated resources for limitranger constraints - Limit ranger should only apply to requested resize. If it considers allocated resources, it's possible to get around the restrictions when down-scaling.

BTW, I missed the last 2 cases in the original PR because they're both operating on the unversioned API, and I was looking for references to `AllocatedResources` on the versioned API.

`pull-kubernetes-e2e-gce-cos-alpha-features` is failing because it's bumping up against the 3 hour time limit. This is due to the large number of resize tests, and how long the tests take. Resizing is currently slow due to the way the PLEG only picks up resized resources from PodSync (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/123940). To speed up the tests, the rollback resize is only tested on a small subset of the tests, which should cut runtime by a little less than half. I also changed the pods to use a generated name to avoid collisions with an asynchronous delete.

issue_context.title: [FG:InPlacePodVerticalScaling] e2e test does not verify resource update in pod status
issue_context.body:
### What happened?

e2e tests for pod resizing does not verify if resources in a pod status is updated to the same values in a pod spec after resizing is actuated. This is caused because the result of the runtime support check is reversed:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/1519f802816f6a6b9bd4cfb259c93644fe950e0e/test/e2e/node/pod_resize.go#L501-L513


### What did you expect to happen?

Resources in pod status are verified.


### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Run e2e test with enabling InPlacePodVerticalScaling.


### Anything else we need to know?

I'm not sure if we should fix it immediately. If this issue is fixed, it will take much longer to finish the tests because there are some issues that it takes much time (60-90s) till resources in a pod status is updated after resizing is actuated such as #123940 and #125559. In addition, pod resize e2e tests are being migrated to e2e node tests in PR #124296.

master branch

review_comments: Just to verify my understanding, the original code here copies the allocated resources from the previous status. We don't need this anymore because `GetContainerResourceAllocation` should always return the latest status?
Correct. I can't think of any reason the old status would ever have AllocatedResources set if the resources aren't in the allocated resources cache.

If there are multiple resize requests, the 1st is in-progress while the 2nd one is yet to be admitted by kubelet, this would clear the status, so users see:
 - desired != allocated
 - allocated == actual
 - resize status: empty

On the other hand, if the resize status is in "Proposed" (and not clobbered by kubelet), users see
 - desired != allocated
 - allocated == actual
 - resize status: proposed

The "proposed" status is not useful at all. Users should simply check the desired/allocated/actual status to understand if a request has been actuated(?).
Trying to figure out how users should interpret the resize status:
 1. Proposed: not meaningful. Check the resource values to understand more. (potentially desired != allocated)
 2. InProgress: some resizing request is in progress (can also be derived from allocated != actual)
 3. Deferred: kubelet's trying to see if it can admit a resized pod (can also be derived from desired != allocated)
 4. Infeasible: kubelet cannot admit a version of the resized pod
 5. "" (empty): kubelet's not currently working any resize request (even if there might be a new desired value)

So a pod can be in a more than one status (e.g., in-progress and deferred) theoretically. I wonder if these would be better surfaced as pod conditions instead -- some of them can be independent and we don't have to check on previous values. 
Discussed over chat. I agree with your analysis, but for v1.32 proceed with it as-is and document the issues, and look into improvements in v1.33. We may not be able to fully resolve this without something like the synchronous admission proposed in https://docs.google.com/document/d/1O9rDeYhGWMbtg-DQmhqKvNsQSHWJSwvSEeNpXTKMvZg/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.6ggs708p6vvu
Yep, we'll have to work around the limitations of the current design for 1.32. Feel free to resolve this comment. 

cc @thockin and @dchen1107 FYI.

Hmm...It's not very intuitive to have resource status set for a terminated pod/container (and the "created" pod case is similar too). These fields neither reflect the desired spec or the actual status. This is basically the targeted allocated resources. Do we have to mix the two?

For non-running containers, it's important for the scheduler to know the allocated resources, but for running containers it should prefer the actual resources. In practice, the distinction for running containers doesn't matter much, but https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/117765 summarizes the reasoning behind it.

Not mixing them goes back to the API questions that we went back and forth on ([summarized here](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1259qZ2cwnsFKe04eUNSC0ZV2uqz4w-_e0Fy_v6G7jA8/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.pjrqqlyd63l4)), but would also add complexity to the resource calculation (if it's not running, use AcceptedResources, if it is running use Resources).

Conceptually, I think it makes sense to just think of the field as the resources that the container is using, or will be using if it's not running (it's a bit funky for terminal containers though).

WDYT?

> (it's a bit funky for terminal containers though).

Yeah the fact that the pod itself is terminated and we still show resource status of the terminated container is weird. So other components will have to condition on the pod status when they calculate the resource usage anyway. 

I don't want to rehash the API discussion since the current proposal already went through extensive reviews, but yeah it does make the meaning of the field vague and conditional :\

Feel free to resolve the comment.
I'll take a note to pay extra attention to this in the documentation. Thanks!
